extracted.intended_audience: readers of Charles Lamb; literary friends, writers, critics, and students of early-19th-century letters and theatre
extracted.subtask_description: Personal, essayistic correspondence that mixes private news, literary criticism, theatrical anecdotes, and comic asides; includes implicit guidance about reviewing, playwriting, staging, and the habits of composition. Useful for writers and critics learning rhetorical and practical norms of early-19th-century literary life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conjecturing when materials are scanty
rubrics_metrics.description: (on Godwin's 'Life of Chaucer') a considerable error runs through it, which is a conjecturing spirit, a fondness for filling out the picture by supposing what Chaucer did and how he felt, where the materials are scanty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overfill gaps in biography or literary history with speculative reconstruction; prefer clear evidence to imaginative filling-out. Criticism grounded in slender materials should avoid expansive conjecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review should grasp the whole, not only parts
rubrics_metrics.description: I can vehemently applaud, or perversely stickle, at parts; but I cannot grasp at a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A competent review or critical account should aim for a methodical, comprehensive sense of the work rather than reacting only to isolated passages. Beware a reviewing habit that praises or quibbles at fragments without accounting for overall structure or intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve detailed criticism for private or direct discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: I am never very fond of saying things before third persons... something is sure to be dropped. I declined naming this fault until I had seen you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offering delicate or potentially contentious critique, discuss it privately or face-to-face rather than airing it in mixed company to avoid misreporting and misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habit and practice produce mechanical command in composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any work which I take upon myself as an engagement will act upon me to torment... The same, till by habit I have acquired a mechanical command, I have felt in making paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphing, regular composition, and meeting commissions become reliable through repeated practice; accept that initial efforts may be difficult and that technique is formed by habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managers (producers) are the decisive judges of a theatrical piece
rubrics_metrics.description: The managers... are the best judges of pieces, and it would be insensible in me to affect a false modesty, after the very flattering letter which I have received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aiming to have a play produced, recognize managers' central role and subjective tastes; be prepared for their caprice and for their authority over acceptance and staging decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be ready to revise when managers request alterations
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece shall be sent to you for your alterations in the course of a few days...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance commonly entails suggested alterations; authors should expect and accommodate editorial or managerial revisions rather than assuming a finished piece will be staged unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject must be substantial for popular audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: It was precisely this flatness, this slightness of plot and catastrophe, that doomed 'Mr. H.' to failure... John Bull must have solider fare than a letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For popular (e.g., 'John Bull') audiences, lightweight or overly slight subjects risk failure; ensure the plot and stakes are sufficiently substantial and satisfying for the expected audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid too many principal characters that fragment the play
rubrics_metrics.description: There were no less than eleven principal characters... and true it was, for Mr. Powell... had all parts equally prominent... and here they all had their ten-minute speeches... which first set the audience a-gaping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the cast of principal characters focused; too many equally prominent figures disperse attention and prevent audience engagement with hero/heroine trajectories. Maintain clear dramatic focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting and actors' quality determine reception
rubrics_metrics.description: His part... was most unluckily Goldfinch... De Camp was hooted, more than hissed... the remainder of his part was forced to be... omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a well-written role can fail if assigned to an unsuitable performer; casting and actors' manner strongly influence public reception. Consider actors' strengths when writing or producing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid offending prevailing moral sensibilities on stage
rubrics_metrics.description: A strumpet was another principal character,--a most unfortunate choice in this moral day. The audience were as scandalized as if you were to introduce such a personage to their private tea-tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sensitive to the morality of your audience and the era; certain character-types or explicit immorality may provoke scandal and damage a play's reception. Tailor content to public tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived borrowing or repetition from other plays harms reception
rubrics_metrics.description: Half the audience did not know that H. had written it, but were displeased at his stealing from the 'Road to Ruin;' and those who might have loved it did not relish the intolerable vulgarity and inanity of the idea stripped of his manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid obvious echoes or apparent plagiarism from recent, well-known plays; audiences resent re-used material, especially when the original manner is absent. Strive for distinctiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staging details and delivery can decide success
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole depends on the manner in which the name is brought out, which I value myself on, as a chef d'oeuvre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small staging choices and actor delivery (timing, emphasis, the way a name or gag is presented) can be decisive; attend carefully to theatrical business and performative detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use secrecy in rehearsal to prevent premature judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The rehearsals have gone on privately, lest by many folks knowing it, the story should come out, which would infallibly damn it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep rehearsals and casting confidential when appropriate to prevent gossip, misjudgment, or premature exposure that might prejudice managers or audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define terms when discussing poetry or criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing like defining of terms when we talk. What blunders might I have fallen into of quite inapplicable criticism, but for this timely explanation!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the specific person or text you mean before launching critical comments; ambiguous names or references can provoke misunderstanding and lead to inapplicable criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: A prologue or ancillary piece can achieve independent success
rubrics_metrics.description: It [the prologue] was received with such shouts as I never witnessed to a prologue. It was attempted to be encored...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ancillary elements (prologues, epilogues, speeches) can win popular favor even if the main piece fails; craft these elements carefully as they may shape immediate audience response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your audience's palate; subtlety often needs a discerning public
rubrics_metrics.description: Brawn... Its gusto is of that hidden sort. As Wordsworth sings of a modest poet, 'you must love him, ere to you he will seem worthy of your love.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some works (or tastes) are subtle and require a receptive, discerning audience; expect that not all pleasures will have immediate or broad appeal. Tailor level of subtlety to intended readers/viewers.
